segments.title: Chương 76: 0076 [Bắc Đại cũng tạm được]
segments.content:
The Southern Media Group was developing rapidly last year.

Especially as it extended its feelers into Beijing and Shanghai!

The feeler reaching into the capital was called *Xinjing*.

The feeler reaching into the magical metropolis was called *Dongzao*.

*Xinjing* had just been founded and was in desperate need of a breakthrough. This time, it followed the South in stirring up trouble.

*Dongzao* was the predecessor of The Paper. Its successive leaders were either dismissed or investigated. But at this point, its notoriety was not yet apparent. The editor-in-chief was from the Southern Media Group, the deputy editor was from *Wenhui Bao*, and its affiliated unit was a Shanghai newspaper group.

They planned to go against the Southern Media Group's headquarters and support the special admission of special talents, including Chen Guiliang. It was also possible they were playing good cop, bad cop, with sister units taking opposing sides to stir up hot topics together.

*Dongzao* asked Chen Guiliang a few more questions to confirm the authenticity of his middle school deeds.

Then, the press conference concluded. After lunch, they still had to tour other parts of the school.

Chen Guiliang and his classmates also headed to the cafeteria. He was surrounded by his brothers from Dorm 302, and the neighboring Dorm 301 also came to join the fun. A dozen or so boys talked animatedly, their faces glowing as they recounted what had just happened.

Bian Guanyue was too embarrassed to squeeze in, simply walking silently alongside Wu Meng.

However, the topic most students discussed was related to the textbook errors.

"Do you guys think the Chinese textbook will be revised?"

"I think it definitely will. So many media outlets are going to report on it."

"I don't think so. In middle school, I even found an error in a history textbook. Hasn't it remained unchanged all these years?"

"How do you know it hasn't been changed?"

"During the New Year, I specifically looked at my cousin's history book."

"If they really do revise the textbook, Daxia Chen will be a legend!"

"..."

The crowd quickened their pace towards the cafeteria, wanting to be the first in line for food before school was out.

The time for lunch was too short!

Chen Guiliang hadn't even finished his meal when his PHS phone rang. It was Tao Xue.

"Big nephew, how did you do today?" Tao Xue asked.

Chen Guiliang replied, "I didn't lose face for Auntie Xue."

Tao Xue sighed, "Ah, I wanted to feign illness and ask for leave, but my homeroom teacher wouldn't approve. I couldn't see you being interviewed by the reporters in person. Where are you?"

"The cafeteria."

In less than a minute, Tao Xue rushed into the cafeteria. She had been on her way.

Tao Xue looked around and quickly spotted the students from Class 11 of the senior year.

"Senior sister!"

Tao Xue didn't greet Chen Guiliang directly but walked over to Bian Guanyue first.

"Hello," Bian Guanyue said.

Tao Xue smiled, "My big nephew is pretty amazing, right?"

"Very impressive."

Bian Guanyue thought to herself: *What big nephew? He's my son.*

Xie Yang had already finished his lunch quickly. Seeing Tao Xue appear, he went over and added fuel to the fire, "You have no idea, Daxia Chen was so freaking awesome today. Let me tell you..."

Tao Xue didn't go to line up for food, just stood there listening to Xie Yang's account. After just a few sentences, her eyes lit up, and she regretted not skipping class to be there in person.

Xu Haibo also joined in, vividly describing what had happened earlier.

Tao Xue listened attentively. She planned to go back to her own class and help promote Chen Guiliang a bit more. And she would emphasize that Daxia Chen was her nephew!

Half an hour later, the senior year afternoon self-study session began.

Bian Guanyue kept turning her head, frequently looking towards the second-to-last row.

The more attention Chen Guiliang received, the more embarrassed she felt to act too close to him. She even felt a faint sense of inferiority, thinking her academic performance was too poor, that she was somewhat unworthy of the brilliant Daxia Chen.

It might seem strange to an adult, but for a high school student, it seemed like a very normal state of mind.

"Why don't you just sit backwards? That way you won't sprain your neck," Wu Meng joked.

Bian Guanyue became haughty again, putting on a cold expression and sitting bolt upright to work on her practice paper.

Chen Guiliang's PHS phone rang again, and it was a long-distance call. "Hello, hello, wait a moment, the signal is bad in the classroom, I'm going out to find a signal... Hello, what did you say... It's Director Cheng... Hello, you should probably just call the emergency contact number."

Damn it, I should buy a mobile phone.

Chen Guiliang came to the front door of the classroom, calling and waving to Bian Guanyue who was sitting in the first row.

Bian Guanyue heard his voice and immediately got up and walked out. She received the call before she had even left the classroom.

"Give me the phone," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue quickly handed it over.

"Hello, Director Cheng, this is Chen Guiliang."

"You haven't been affected by the public opinion, have you?"

"I'm fine."

"There's a lot of noise in society right now, and some people at our Peking University are also against it. But independent admissions are precisely for selecting outstanding talents. As long as this principle remains unchanged, we are not afraid of any criticism. After a school meeting and discussion, the conditions for your special admission have been determined."

"Please go ahead, Director Cheng."

"As long as you pass the Tier 1 cutoff score in the Gaokao, Peking University can admit you. Also, you don't need to come for the independent admissions exam. Just supplement your application materials and mail them in. I'll read you the mailing address."

"Wait, let me get a pen and paper."

"It's fine even if it gets lost in the mail. I'll call and ask you to resend it."

Chen Guiliang returned to his seat to jot down the address, then asked, "Director Cheng, can I choose the philosophy department at your university?"

Director Cheng: "Why not the Chinese department?"

"I'm more interested in philosophy." Chen Guiliang had already boasted, so naturally, he couldn't go back on his word. He felt it didn't matter which major he chose.

And he did genuinely like philosophy.

Twenty years from now, Fudan's philosophy program would be second to none.

But in the just-passed year of 2003, the top five for philosophy were: Wuhan University, Peking University, Nanjing University, Renmin University, Fudan University.

This year's rankings wouldn't be out until July, and the top five for philosophy were about to become: Peking University, Renmin University, Nanjing University, Wuhan University, Fudan University.

No matter how you ranked it, Fudan was always number five.

"You can study in the philosophy department," Director Cheng readily agreed, as the philosophy department was also under his purview.

Chen Guiliang asked again, "Does this need to be kept confidential?"

Director Cheng said, "No need. The list will be publicly announced soon, and the media will definitely be watching. It'll be the same whether you keep it confidential or not. Are you certain you want to come to Peking University?"

"Certain."

"Good, I'll be waiting for your application materials. Make sure to send it by EMS express delivery, the expedited service. Remember, the expedited one. Don't skimp on postage, to avoid it getting lost."

"I'll send it out today."

After hanging up, Chen Guiliang found that not only was Bian Guanyue looking at him, but students in the surrounding seats were all looking over as well.

His deskmate Qin Shanshan glanced at the address he had written down. "Peking University?"

"Peking University is not bad," Chen Guiliang nodded.

Bian Guanyue had a smile on her face, her expression full of admiration.

Qin Shanshan shouted at the top of her lungs, "Daxia Chen is going to Peking University!"

The quiet afternoon self-study session immediately erupted into a clamor, and many students left their seats.

Guan Zhiqiang, holding a novel, grinned at Li Jun. "Huo huo."

"Huo your mother!"

Li Jun was extremely annoyed. He even wanted to find a reporter and expose the fact that Chen Guiliang had been put on probation.

But Li Jun didn't dare. The guy was always a coward when it mattered.

Guan Zhiqiang smiled without a word. He had already passed the art major exam and was 100% certain to get into a well-known art academy.

And Li Jun?

Heh, he could obediently go to a junior college!

Peking University's independent admissions program had started last year.

Before that, there was a lack of transparent rules; the school could recruit however it wanted. Now, not only were detailed procedures established, but a public announcement stage was also added—this was an important part of the admissions reform.

For the first year of independent admissions, Peking University was given 150 spots. But to be cautious, Peking University voluntarily reduced the number to 50.

This year was the second year of independent admissions, and the deadline had actually already passed.

According to the normal procedure, application materials should have been submitted before December 20th of last year, with interviews and written exams in mid-January—which happened to be during the New Concept Essay Competition rematch period.

Major universities made an exception for the first-prize winners of the competition, allowing them to submit their materials late, and some universities even required a supplementary written test.

In addition, later independent admissions programs allowed for a score reduction of 20-60 points for admission. But at this time, independent admissions were stricter; in principle, only a 20-point reduction was allowed, and special cases required a meeting for discussion.

"Class president, I'd like to ask for leave to mail my materials to Peking University," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Rui nodded repeatedly, "Go ahead, it's fine."

Amid the envious gazes of his classmates, Chen Guiliang left the classroom with the materials he had long prepared.

Tsinghua hadn't called yet, and Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered to wait any longer.

Since Peking University had confirmed special admission as long as he passed the Tier 1 cutoff, and Chen Guiliang was confident he could, Peking University was naturally the top choice.

Especially for studying philosophy, Fudan at this time was too "lame." Perennially number five!

Chen Guiliang also borrowed Bian Guanyue's mobile phone. On his way to the post office, he called back Fudan, Beijing Normal University, and other universities one by one, expressing his apologies and regrets.

Meanwhile, after Chen Guiliang left, the class president Li Rui ran to report to their homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying.

Upon receiving the news, Liu Shuying immediately went to report to the principal.

Principal Yan was accompanying media reporters on a tour. He was stunned for a moment, then announced with a smile, "Our school's student, Chen Guiliang, has been offered special admission by Peking University as long as he meets the Tier 1 cutoff."

The dozens of reporters grew even more excited. Another news point!

Even if Principal Yan hadn't said anything, Peking University would be announcing the list soon anyway.

Chen Guiliang's admission to Peking University was not 100% certain. He had to pass the Tier 1 cutoff in the Gaokao, so he still had to continue studying hard.

Magical Metropolis, *Sprout* magazine office.

Editor-in-chief Zhao Changtian was at his wit's end. Major universities were calling one after another, all canceling their score reduction admission spots for next year.

Not a single spot was being given to the New Concept Competition!

They said the public opinion pressure was too great, and they had to lie low for a while and find another opportunity to resume in the future.

The problem was, if it was interrupted for even one year, the number of participants would surely plummet, and it would never recover even if it was reinstated.

Hu Weishi knocked and came in. "A submission from Chen Guiliang."

"A short story?" Zhao Changtian asked.

"It's a bit like a thesis, but the format is wrong," Hu Weishi said, not knowing whether to laugh or cry.

She had received all kinds of submissions, but this was the first time she had encountered a thesis. She didn't even know which section to publish it in.

The content of the article was precisely about questioning the errors in the textbook version of "Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng." Chen Guiliang had mailed it out last week.

Moreover, Chen Guiliang deliberately feigned immaturity and concealed his skills, acting like he had never seen a professional thesis before and completely disregarding the standard format for papers. On one hand, this suited his identity as a high school student; on the other, it could make the article more interesting and lower the barrier to entry for readers.

Zhao Changtian asked, "What's your plan?"

Hu Weishi said, "In the latest issue of *Sprout*, in the selected award-winning works section, we'll publish Chen Guiliang's 'Yinghai Xing.' As for this article, we'll publish it in the 'Campus Scan' section."

Zhao Changtian nodded and said, "The public opinion right now is too fierce and complex. *Sprout* publishing two articles that are not very entertaining but have decent literary and academic merit can help restore our image. Publish them!"

Publishing articles naturally meant paying fees.

"Yinghai Xing" was a poem, and the payment standard was different.

All told, Chen Guiliang could probably get over 6,000 yuan in fees for the two articles.

In addition, there was a gold prize for the essay competition.

Even among first-prize winners, the prize money varied, with the highest being 5,000 yuan.

Chen Guiliang's "Yinghai Xing" was rated as exceptionally outstanding, and the prize money was temporarily increased to 6,000 yuan. He was the only one!

With his exceptionally outstanding first-prize essay and the fees for two articles, his total income had now reached over 12,000 yuan.

When the selected works from the New Concept Competition were published, Chen Guiliang could collect another fee.

In an era when the publishing industry had not yet collapsed, writing was truly profitable!

Zhao Changtian called over the general director of the New Concept Competition, Li Qigang, "There are no score reduction admission spots for next year. We can only increase the prize money to attract young people to participate."

"How much should we raise the prize money to?" Li Qigang asked.

Zhao Changtian said, "The highest prize will be ten thousand yuan!"

On March 1st, the latest issue of *Sprout* hit the stands, publishing both of Chen Guiliang's articles.

Furthermore, the cover featured a massive headline: "Award-winning masterpiece by young literary genius Chen Guiliang!"

The single-issue sales of this magazine had long surpassed 500,000 copies.

And these were all bought with students' own money. One magazine could be passed around half a class.

Over the next half a month, Chen Guiliang's articles would be read by at least two or three million students.

(Thanks to the user 青灯古佛一盏老酒一支烟 for the Alliance Lord level donation.)

(According to the number of reader votes, Peking University was the undisputed first, with Fudan only getting half the votes of Peking University. Therefore, Daxia Chen chooses Peking University.)
